data.title: Implement and validate amend mapping expectations
data.when: When a new 'amend' or update functionality requires defining a structured data mapping that involves complex state changes.
procedure: 1. Review the existing domain models to identify the primary source and target schemas for the amendment mapping.
2. Draft the core mapping logic, ensuring all necessary fields and relationships are defined in the new configuration file.
3. Critically analyze the system's assumptions about data state before and after the amendment is applied (the 'expectation').

4. Explicitly add or correct any required expectation configurations that govern how partial updates or conditional mapping logic must behave, preventing default fallback behavior from causing runtime errors.
5. Execute localized unit tests specifically targeting boundary conditions (e.g., null values, missing optional fields) to validate the amended mappings.
pitfalls: The mapping compiles successfully but fails at runtime due to an unstated or incorrect expectation regarding data state (e.g., assuming a field is populated when it should be nullable).
The task assumes simple one-to-one field correspondence, leading to missed transformation logic for complex types.
verification: All unit tests involving the amendment mapping pass without exception.
Manual verification confirms that the system handles partial updates correctly according to the specified business rules, and no escalation was required during local testing.
